name: The Fall of the Romanovs and the Rise of Stalin
description: How Russia went from freeing its serfs to a workers' state ruled by one man: the last tsar, a lost war, two revolutions in one year, civil war, and Stalin's grip on power.

checkpoints.name: Serfs and socialists
checkpoints.note: The House of Romanov rules the Russian Empire from Saint Petersburg. The emancipation reform of 1861 frees the serfs but leaves many of them poor and in debt. Karl Marx co-writes The Communist Manifesto in 1848, and by the 1880s Marxism is winning converts among Russian radicals.

checkpoints.name: The last tsar
checkpoints.note: Nicholas II takes the throne in 1894 and pushes the Trans-Siberian Railway east. Defeat in the Russo-Japanese War sets off the Russian Revolution of 1905, and the tsar grants a parliament. Vladimir Lenin leads the Bolshevik wing of the Marxists, which becomes its own party and launches Pravda in 1912.

checkpoints.name: War and two revolutions
checkpoints.note: Russia enters World War I and loses an army at Tannenberg in 1914. Hunger and defeat bring down the monarchy in February 1917, and Nicholas II abdicates. In October Lenin's Bolsheviks, organised by Leon Trotsky, seize power in Petrograd in the Russian Revolution.

checkpoints.name: Civil war
checkpoints.note: Lenin signs the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk, giving up vast lands to make peace with Germany, and moves the capital to Moscow and the Kremlin. The tsar and his family are shot. Trotsky builds the Red Army, which wins the Russian Civil War, and the Soviet Union is founded at the end of 1922.

checkpoints.name: Stalin takes control
checkpoints.note: A new Soviet ruble steadies the economy. After Lenin dies in 1924, Joseph Stalin outmanoeuvres Trotsky and drives him into exile, while Sergei Eisenstein's Battleship Potemkin celebrates 1905. Forced collectivisation brings the Holodomor famine, the Moscow trials destroy the old Bolsheviks, and Trotsky is murdered in 1940.
